title: Angle Trisection OQ02-OQ03 Extension: Gauss-Wantzel Arithmetic Bridge — OQ extension (01)

problemStatement.plain: Formal mathematical investigation: Angle Trisection OQ02-OQ03 Extension: Gauss-Wantzel Arithmetic Bridge — OQ extension (01).

currentState.focus: Doubling invariance of TotientIsPow2 — shipped PR #29331.

knowledge.progressSummary: Isolated the role of the prime 2 in the Gauss–Wantzel arithmetic bridge: proved TotientIsPow2 (2n) ↔ TotientIsPow2 n and its 2-power generalization, reducing constructibility to the odd part of n. 11 thm / 1 def / 159L, verified 0-axiom. PR #29331.
builtItems: totient_pow2_two_pow_mul_iff: TotientIsPow2 (2^a·n) ↔ TotientIsPow2 n (reduction to odd part)
insights: The prime 2 splits φ(2n) by parity: 2φ(n) for even n, φ(n) for odd n (Nat.totient_mul_of_prime_of_{dvd,not_dvd}); both preserve the power-of-2 property, so 2 is 'free' in Gauss–Wantzel.
Doubling iff forward direction is the non-trivial one: from 2φ(n)=2^k deduce k≥1 and φ(n)=2^(k-1); reverse is angle bisection.
Constructibility of a regular n-gon depends only on the odd part of n; combined with the parent's coprime multiplicativity this reduces the whole criterion to odd prime powers.
Bisection can never create constructibility: a single odd-base computation (φ(7)=2·3, φ(15)=2^3) propagates to all 2^a multiples via the invariance.
mathlibGaps: No direct doubling/2-power-invariance lemma for the power-of-2-totient predicate in Mathlib; built from the prime-multiplicativity totient lemmas.
nextSteps: Assemble TotientIsPow2 n ↔ (n = 2^a × distinct Fermat primes) as a single biconditional using this invariance + the parent's odd-prime-factor / Fermat analysis.
Explicit Bool decision procedure operating only on the odd part.
